items.title: The Hits Keep On Coming: Dolphins’ Jordan Phillips Suffers Season-Ending Injury
items.text:
Miami loses its third defensive tackle to a season-ending injury in two weeks.
The Miami Dolphins’ defensive line suffered another major blow Tuesday, with defensive tackle Jordan Phillips becoming the third member of the unit to suffer a season-ending injury in the span of two weeks.
ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reported that Phillips suffered a torn biceps during Sunday’s loss to the Indianapolis Colts and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. The Dolphins subsequently placed Phillips on injured reserve.
The Dolphins lost veteran defensive tackle Zach Sieler to a ruptured biceps in their Week 9 loss to the Detroit Lions. Zeek Biggers suffered a knee injury against Indianapolis and will undergo season-ending surgery to repair the lateral meniscus in his right knee.
With Sieler, Phillips, Biggers and Grant leading the way, the Dolphins have climbed to 10th in the NFL in total defense and 10th in rushing yards allowed per carry. Those rankings could take a significant hit with three of the four players now sidelined for the remainder of the season.
Phillips, a fifth-round selection in the 2025 NFL Draft, had emerged as an important piece of Miami’s defensive line. The 22-year-old appeared in all nine games this season, recording 28 tackles and a tackle for loss while playing approximately 60 percent of the team’s defensive snaps.
His importance to the defense went beyond the statistics. Phillips had become a reliable run defender, occupying blockers and allowing Miami’s linebackers to make plays. He was expected to take on an even larger role following Sieler’s injury, with head coach Jeff Hafley previously identifying him as someone who needed to step up and provide leadership to the defensive line.
Instead, Miami will have to move forward without all three of its most heavily used defensive tackles.
With Phillips and Biggers joining Sieler on injured reserve, the Dolphins are left with Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. as their primary defensive tackles. Miami promoted Jordan Jefferson from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday and also signed former Dolphins defensive tackle Matthew Butler and Chris Smith to the practice squad.
The timing of these injuries couldn’t be much worse. Miami travels to Buffalo in Week 11 to face a Bills offense averaging more than 150 rushing yards per game, with James Cook among the league’s leading rushers. The Dolphins will need their remaining defensive linemen to find a way to replace the production of three players who had become central to their defensive success.
items.desc: Miami loses its third defensive tackle to a season-ending injury in two weeks.

items.title: Coast Guard offloads over $18M worth of cocaine at Miami Beach station; 3 detained
items.text:
MIAMI BEACH, FLA. (WSVN) - The U.S. Coast Guard offloaded millions of dollars worth of cocaine at its Miami Beach station on Tuesday.
A cutter crew intercepted a boat off the coast of Jamaica and seized over 2,400 pounds of cocaine, worth over $18 million.

items.title: Major flooding in South Florida forces Broward officials to close schools Wednesday
items.text:
First responders in Hollywood said they received more than 300 calls for help due to flooding on Tuesday night and Wednesday morning.

Heavy rain pounded communities across South Florida on Tuesday night and into Wednesday morning, and that led to significant flooding that forced officials to close schools and roads in Broward County, led to a hospital suspending visitation for safety reasons and even led to a roof collapse at a synagogue.The dangerous situation began to unfold on Tuesday when rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms began to push into parts of Miami-Dade and Broward counties, and the precipitation refused to let up.Water began to rise as that was occurring, and hundreds of motorists on roads and highways became stranded in floodwaters.First responders were called in to rescue those who were stranded, and crews were forced to block off roads to prevent more motorists from being stranded.Flooding was reported on on-ramps and off-ramps on Interstate 95 in Broward, and water covered the road on the Florida's Turnpike near Hollywood.Ground stop ordered at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International AirportAccording to the Federal Aviation Administration, a ground stop has been ordered at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport due to the weather.According to information provided by the FAA, the ground stop was ordered on Wednesday morning, and there is a medium chance that it could be extended.It's unknown at the time how many flights have been impacted so far.How much rain fell in South Florida so far?Over the past 24 hours, the CBS News Miami NEXT Weather team reported nearly a foot of rain in some spots of Broward County.Near Plantation, about 11.9 inches of rain has fallen over the past 24 hours, and between 8 and 10 inches of rain has fallen across Hollywood.In Fort Lauderdale, about 7 inches of rain has fallen, and more rain is on the way for Wednesday.Lower rain totals were reported in Miami-Dade County, but the region continues to brace for the risk of heavy rain during the day on Wednesday.Broward County Public Schools closed on Wednesday due to widespread flooding"Due to weather conditions, Broward County Public Schools (BCPS) will close all schools and District offices today, Wednesday, November 18, 2026," officials said in a statement. "This closure includes all before- and after-school care programs, extracurricular activities, and District-sponsored events scheduled for today."Officials continued and urged people to exercise caution and stay safe as the region continues to experience flooding from the heavy rain overnight.In addition, officials said that a decision on whether to reopen schools on Thursday will be made later on Wednesday."We appreciate your patience, flexibility, and understanding as we continue to monitor weather conditions," officials said.Heavy rain leads to roof collapse at Hollywood synagogue First responders in Hollywood raced to investigate reports of a roof collapse at a synagogue early Wednesday morning.According to Hollywood Fire-Rescue, the roof of Temple Sinai located at 1400 N. 46th Avenue collapsed due to the heavy rain.Officials said no injuries were reported.Transit service in Broward County remains operational, officials sayDespite flooding across Broward County, officials said transit service remains operational."Broward County Transit (BCT) bus service continues to operate amid heavy rainfall and localized street flooding in some areas of Broward County," officials said in

items.title: Home sales have dropped in Miami-Dade. What’s next for the housing market?
items.text:
Political uncertainty and high mortgage rates likely made buyers more hesitant.

Home sales were down in Miami-Dade last month, likely driven by pre-Election Day uncertainty and high mortgage rates.
In Miami-Dade, total home sales declined 10.6% in October compared to the same time period last year. Single-family sales dropped by 11.8% and condo sales 9.6%, according to a report from the Miami Association of Realtors.
Palm Beach County saw a similar dip, as total home sales fell by 8.3% year-over-year. But home sales in Broward County remained nearly unchanged compared to the previous October.
Alfredo Pujol, the president of the organization, said people have been “waiting and seeing” where mortgage and interest rates would land and how the midterm elections would unfold. Pujol said it’s common to see hesitancy from homebuyers leading up to a consequential election.
While declining year-over-year home sales have become a longer-term trend in South Florida’s softening market, October’s numbers represented a sharper drop. Compared to September, numbers fell significantly in Miami-Dade. Total home sales were down 2% year-over-year in September.
But with elections now behind us, Pujol said, “I do see that there’s going to be a little bit of an uptick.”
With Amendment 3 approved, Pujol said he expects to see people more eager to buy homes, especially around the middle and lower ends of the housing market. The statewide ballot measure, which received about 62% of the vote, will raise the homestead exemption and save many Florida homeowners on their property tax bill.
The amendment will raise the homestead exemption first to $150,000 in 2027 and then to $250,000 in 2028. Florida TaxWatch estimated it will save homesteaded homeowners in the city of Miami around $1,216 in 2027 and $2,448 in 2028, savings more significant to middle-class buyers, Pujol said.
Some out-of-state buyers looking to relocate to Florida may rush to do so before the end of the year because of Amendment 3, Pujol said. That’s because people who move to Florida in January 2027 or later will have to wait five years before they are eligible for the homestead exemption.
High mortgage rates are likely part of what is discouraging homebuyers right now, Pujol said. But he added that mortgage rates have been relatively high for several months, so he doesn’t think that’s the only factor depressing home sales. Mortgage rates have been at or above 7% for more than two months.
But even when high mortgage rates keep some buyers on the sidelines, the luxury market, which generally has more cash buyers, remains more insulated. That has been the case for Miami-Dade over the last few months.
On the higher end of the market, Pujol said he expects to see the factors that have attracted wealthy buyers to Florida — low taxes and business-friendly policies — continue to buoy luxury home sales in the region.
The ultra-luxury segment of the market has been particularly strong this year. It took just eight months this year for Miami-Dade to beat its previous record for $30 million-and-up home sales. Pujol said he expects the trend to continue, with the caveat that inventory at that end of the market is quite limited.
Despite the housing market slump in October, total year-to-date home sales are up in Miami-Dade, according to the Miami Association of Realtors.

items.title: Miami-Dade County, American Airlines reach agreement to protect jobs, expand opportunities at MIA
items.text:
Miami-Dade County and American Airlines have reached a new agreement aimed at protecting hundreds of aviation jobs, expanding business opportunities and supporting future development at Miami International Airport (MIA).
The agreement, approved by Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava and the Board of County Commissioners on Tuesday, Nov. 17, allows the county to acquire Hangar 890, Building 891 and associated property from a third party while ensuring American Airlines retains the facilities needed for its aircraft maintenance operations.
County officials say the arrangement will help modernize airport infrastructure, improve operational efficiency and make strategically important airport property available for future development.
For American Airlines, the agreement preserves long-term maintenance operations at one of its largest international hubs, supporting more than 650 skilled aircraft maintenance positions while providing flexibility for future expansion.
The agreement also supports Miami-Dade County's broader efforts to protect high-paying jobs, encourage investment and strengthen workforce development.
American Airlines is Miami-Dade County's largest private employer, with nearly 16,000 employees locally. Its operations at MIA generate more than $30 billion in annual economic activity and support over 40,000 direct, indirect and induced jobs across the region, according to county officials.
"Miami International Airport is one of our County's greatest economic engines. Partnerships like this ensure we continue turning that strength into opportunity for our residents," said Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava.
"By deepening our longstanding partnership with American Airlines, the anchor partner at MIA, we are protecting and growing hundreds of good-paying aviation jobs, creating new business opportunities, and building a solid foundation for future investment. This is a win for American Airlines, a win for MIA, and most importantly, a win for Miami-Dade County's families, businesses, and future generations."
MIA Director and CEO Ralph Cutié said the agreement would help position the airport for continued growth while strengthening its role as a major economic driver.
"This agreement reflects the value of our longstanding partnership with American Airlines and our shared commitment to MIA's continued success," Cutié said.
"It allows us to plan strategically for future growth, expand business opportunities, and strengthen the infrastructure that supports our airport community. By working together, we are positioning MIA to remain competitive while supporting the economic vitality of Miami-Dade County."
American Airlines Senior Vice President of MIA Operations Juan Carlos Liscano also welcomed the agreement, emphasizing Miami's importance to the airline's international network.
"Miami is a cornerstone of American's international network and a consequential part of our long-term growth strategy," Liscano said.
“This agreement reinforces our dedication to our Miami team and preserves our ability to continue growing our network to more destinations around the world for our customers. We are proud to build on our longstanding relationship with Miami-Dade County, where we are deeply invested in the continued success of this incredible community."
